TITLE: lastAccruedOn gate compares local day to stored UTC day
FILE: src/interest.js
LINE: 23
CATEGORY: correctness
SEVERITY: critical
VERDICT: CONFIRMED
PANEL: 3 of 3 skeptics could not refute it
CORRECTED: True

Verified by running the real code: under TZ=Australia/Sydney (UTC+11), a single open, rate-bearing account was credited interest 12 times within a single UTC calendar day on two consecutive days, instead of once; under TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14) the PR's own added idempotency test (which calls accrueInterest twice with the identical clock) fails, returning {accounts:1, cents:13} on the second call instead of the asserted {accounts:0, cents:0}.

findings.summary: An old (pre-PR) server binary, which this repo's own deploy contract says may run concurrently with the new one during a rollout, strips the new `lastAccruedOn` field from any account row it touches for an ordinary reason (deposit, transfer, close, rate change) — defeating the double-accrual guard this PR relies on.

findings.summary: The new setInterval unconditionally runs accrueInterest(store) + store.save() (a whole-file overwrite) every hour for the lifetime of every server process, turning the documented 'two copies can run against one file during a deploy' window (docs/deploy.md:9) into an automatic, unbounded, recurring last-write-wins clobber instead of the brief, operator-controlled, once-a-day external job it replaces.
findings.failure_scenario: Two Store instances opened against the same ledger file (old and new copies overlapping during a deploy, or a straggling/zombie old copy that has stopped serving traffic but is still alive): process A performs a real write (a deposit, balance 1000 -> 5000) and saves; process B's independent hourly timer then fires accrueInterest(B.store) + B.store.save() against B's stale in-memory snapshot (still 1000), unconditionally overwriting the file back to balanceCents: 1000 even when accrueInterest credited nothing that tick — silently erasing A's deposit with no error raised, since store.save()'s only error path is a failed write, not a stale read.

findings.failure_scenario: On any server process whose local timezone offset from UTC is non-zero (no TZ is pinned anywhere in the repo, Dockerfile, or docs), the hourly accrueInterest() job re-credits the same account multiple times per calendar day, because dayOf(clock()) (local day) is compared against lastAccruedOn (persisted as the UTC day). **Status: complete.** PR #14, head `0bf2391`. Project checks (`npm run check && npm test`) passed clean on the base, so none of this is noise from a broken baseline. No pre-existing findings — all three root causes are this diff's.

Severities, most severe first: `src/interest.js:23` **critical**, `src/store.js:91` **high**, `src/server.js:161` **high**. The first and second both break the PR's central claim, from different directions — the README's "not safe to run twice" line was deleted, but the guard that was supposed to earn that deletion doesn't hold on a non-UTC host, and an old binary mid-deploy wipes the field the guard reads.

**Budget:** used 18 of 20 (ceiling computed by the script: no `--agents` given, 20 being the smallest with room for every fixed angle plus two of the scout's). 1 scout, 6 finders, 1 triage, 9 skeptics (three three-lens panels, none shared), 1 critic. No same-site check was needed and nothing was merged — triage put the 8 raw findings into 3 root causes with no two groups landing at one site. Three agents stalled and were restarted by the runtime (scout, `refute:p1.3`, `refute:p2.1`); none counted against the budget and no agent was retried for a wrong-commit or dead answer.

**Angles:** 6 run — the scout's own *day-boundary idempotency (the PR's central claim)*, plus correctness, boundary-contract, tests-that-dont-test, data-integrity, migrations-and-rollout, all five sharpened at specific code. Three dropped with reasons: *authz-and-attribution* (no new route or entry point; the timer is in-process and attribution is the unchanged `system` actor), *security* (no new injection surface, secrets, or outbound call), *silent-drops* (`lastAccruedOn` is added to `SCHEMA.accounts` in the same change that writes it, and read back under the same name). The ceiling cut nothing; no angle failed.

**Verification:** 0 of 3 root causes refuted, 0 downgraded, 0 left unverified. All three were **corrected** by their skeptics before being upheld — so read the summaries above as the skeptics' versions, not the finders'. Two were upheld 3-of-3 and one split 2-of-3, which is why `src/server.js:161` is PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED. Nothing was dismissed for doubt alone.

**The critic found 3 gaps no angle covered** — never tested against a skeptic, so these are for you to check by hand, not findings:

1. **No catch-up for a day the server is entirely down.** `dailyInterest` always credits a flat one day (`src/interest.js:10-13`) and the trigger is now tied to the app's own uptime (`src/server.js:161-165`). A crash loop or incident spanning local midnight silently drops that day's interest for every account, with no backfill and no log separating "nothing to accrue" from "never ran". The PR traded a decoupled trigger for a less durable one without saying so.
2. **A failed `store.save()` after a successful in-memory accrual is logged, never rolled back** (`src/server.js:162-164`). The gate reads the in-memory `lastAccruedOn`, already advanced before the save attempt, so a transient failure leaves the process believing the account was credited. A restart before the next successful save loses that day's credit from disk with no audit trace.
3. **README's quickstart (line 10, untouched) still tells operators to run `scripts/run-jobs.mjs interest` on an external daily scheduler**, contradicting the section updated 39 lines below. An operator reading only the quickstart gets no signal to retire their cron entry — making the two-scheduler overlap permanent rather than deploy-brief, which is exactly what feeds findings 2 and 3 above.

Result JSON written to `calibration/results/0.4.0/pr-14.json`. All 18 worktrees and their branches removed; your checkout is unchanged — `main` at `7fc1c3c`, clean, `git worktree list` back to just the repo. Nothing posted to the PR, per `--no-post`.
